component.name: Renome
component.summary: Rename many files at once, and undo it

description.p: Renome renames hundreds of files at once. Stack a few rules, see every new name before anything changes, and undo it all from the history, even after closing the app.

ul.li: Rules: replace text, regular expressions, rearrange parts, case, insert dates (including when a photo was taken), numbering, remove characters or ranges
Movies and TV shows named from TMDB in the format Jellyfin, Kodi and Emby recognize
Music named and sorted from its tags, optionally fixed with MusicBrainz
Books named from Open Library, comics from their ComicInfo.xml, file name or a catalog
Files are never overwritten; a rename stopped halfway is recovered on the next start
Built-in manual; interface in English, Portuguese and Spanish

screenshot.caption: Text rules cleaning up episode names, with what changes highlighted
Choosing between two movies with the same title
Songs named and sorted into artist and album folders from their tags
Comics named by series and number, in series folders

description.p: Subtitles can also come from SubSource, are checked against the video's length (one made for another cut is passed over) and are picked better inside zips. The best one is chosen fairly among the services, sparing OpenSubtitles' few downloads a day, and a language already inside the video can still be downloaded as a file. Comic readers are listed by model, grouped by brand and line, newest first. A text size option makes the whole window larger.

Comics and books made into AZW3 now open on Kindles: they show their cover in the library and go back to it after the last page. Comic e-books can be KEPUB, fitted CBZ or PDF, for about 25 reader screens, with contrast, enlarging, 16 greys, split or turned double pages, webtoon strips, joined volumes and books in parts. Converted books are checked against other tools: FB2 is always valid, the language is guessed from the text when missing, and old encodings of text and subtitles are recognised better.

Movies and episodes get everything their .nfo holds written inside MKV and MP4 videos: cast with characters, directors, writers, age rating, collection, trailer and the background picture. The details that came with a video can be removed first, and audio and subtitle tracks can be named by language, telling apart two dubs or subtitles of the same language. On Windows, subtitle tools, book polish and video details work again.

Books convert between formats, and details are written into AZW3, MOBI and FB2. A new rule cleans, converts and retimes subtitles and takes them out of MKV videos. The same movie, episode, comic or book in several files is found, with the best one marked. Movie and episode details and the cover can be written inside MKV and MP4 videos. Comics become e-books for readers. OpenSubtitles and SubDL keys are kept again.

Subtitles can be downloaded for movies and TV shows from OpenSubtitles and SubDL. A catalogue link or id can be pasted in any search. Song tags, book details, comic details and photo dates can be typed by hand. Undo shows its progress and can be stopped.
Photos and phone videos are named and sorted into folders by when they were taken. Similar pictures are found and compared side by side, and a file's cover is compared with the catalogue's covers.
Comics can be looked up on Metron (also by barcode), AniList and MangaUpdates, and anime on AniList. Books can be looked up on Google Books too, with your own free key.

The comic rule can also convert to CBZ the EPUB, MOBI and AZW3 files made only of pictures (comics and manga from stores, without DRM) and folders of pictures, which are renamed as items. Title and author of EPUB and Kindle files can go into ComicInfo.xml.

The comic rule can write ComicInfo.xml inside CBZ files and the book rule the details inside EPUB files, with undo. Comics in CBR, CB7 and CBT, and PDFs, can be converted to CBZ, keeping the original beside or sending it to the trash. PDF pages keep their pictures as they are; pages that are more than one picture are drawn, or the PDF can be left as it is.

What other programs already recorded is used before searching by name: the .nfo files Jellyfin, Kodi and Emby keep beside movies and in show folders (TMDB or IMDb ids), the metadata.opf of library managers beside books, and the MetronInfo.xml or ComicBookInfo details inside comics.

Templates have many more fields: a movie's genre, country, director, studio, collection and age rating; a show's network and absolute episode number; edition, source and release group from video file names; release dates with the month's name; a book's language and pages; and a comic's story arc, colorist, letterer, cover artist, imprint, scanner and more. Online answers are kept on disk for the days chosen in Options, so searching the same files again is instant. Only one lookup rule (movie, show, music, book or comic) is used at a time, and the optional columns show only those that fit it.

The Extension rule can set each file's extension from what it really is: a .jpg that is a PNG becomes .png, a .cbz that is a RAR becomes .cbr, a file with no extension gets one, and a text file named .pdf becomes .txt (or keeps a fitting extension already in its name, like movie.nfo). Templates can name a fallback, {title|year}, and the number of digits, {episode:3}. Comic details are read from archives whose extension does not match their type.

Artwork and .nfo files a media server left in a movie's folder now go with the movie to its new folder, also when copying or moving to another folder. Forced subtitles named with a dash keep their flag. The Rename button no longer counts a cover an album folder already has, and Discogs covers embedded in songs follow the cover size chosen.

The list can show columns with what the files hold (artist, album, track, length, format, resolution, codec, photo date), sortable and exported. Discogs, with your personal token, finds albums MusicBrainz does not have. Songs repeated in other files (same title, artist and length) are marked. Keys, tokens and the Grand Comics Database account, now set in Options, are kept encrypted in the system's password store. Undo of written tags brings back fields other programs wrote, every field is now written in every format, and the missing rows can be hidden. Sticks formatted for Windows are recognised on Linux in more cases. On macOS checkboxes show and the title bar follows the theme; macOS 11 or newer is required.

Files can be moved or copied to another folder, even on another disk, with progress, Stop and an undo that keeps copies you changed. Templates gain optional parts shown only when their fields have values, more music fields (original year, label, catalog number, format, bitrate, sort names, initial) and resolution and video codec for movies and series. A new rule converts characters: fixes broken accents, transliterates to Latin letters and makes web-safe names. The Remove rule can drop leading numbers and limit name length, and downloaded covers can be 1200, 500 or 250 pixels.

Shows the tracks missing from an album, the movies missing from a collection and the volumes missing from a book series, with CSV export. Renaming never replaces a file on macOS and Windows either. On Windows, hidden and system files stay out of the list and the title bar follows the theme. Playlists use forward slashes everywhere, and writing tags keeps the encoder field.

Online searches can be stopped, keeping what was found. If the program stops while writing tags, the next start cleans up and keeps the songs written undoable. On Linux, names a USB stick formatted for Windows refuses are flagged before renaming. AcoustID retries a dropped connection.

Folders: when files move to a new folder next to their old one, the old folder is deleted if empty or renamed "(additional files)" if files stay, for movies, shows, music, books and comics. A folder holding one movie, album, comic series or book is taken as its own, whatever its name. The Folder column shows where each file goes, and files a lookup rule does not handle are tagged.

Comics: missing issues show up as faded rows (between your files on MangaDex); the series picker narrows by year and publisher; GCD variant covers count as one issue. Clear forgets past lookups, and windows no longer close on an outside click.
Movie and TV show rules touch only videos and subtitles; "Part II" matches "Part 2"; every season in one folder is matched by title; missing episodes can be exported to CSV.

TV shows: aired episodes missing from your seasons show up as faded rows; a folder mixing several shows is looked up show by show; files named after another show are no longer matched to the one searched.
An optional tip link in the status bar and the About tab. Renome stays free.
Album playlists are made even when the album has a cue sheet; a rule turned off can no longer be changed or searched with.
The Folder column shows where a file goes; complete license texts; every data source credited.
Renames and undos stopped halfway are recovered; the window keeps responding during long work; the list works from the keyboard.
